clue.text: Remarkable auxiliary ecclesiastic

parts.note: an auxiliary is something additional, an extra
an ordinary is a church official, such as a bishop, with authority over a diocese

explanation.surface: A deputy clergyman turns out to be quite something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ecclesiastic' looks like part of the picture, but it is the churchman known as an ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the common run is unusual, striking or remarkable.

clue.text: Test most of legal argument, for instance

parts.note: an exam is a test

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: a plea is an argument made in a court of law

explanation.surface: A trial lawyer quizzes a witness about most of his case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' trims PLEA to PLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A case that illustrates a general rule is an illustrative instance.

clue.text: Plate semi-developed in such photography

indicators.note: film is developed into pictures, and these letters are developed into a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A photographic plate half-processed in a certain kind of photography.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' rearranges SEMI and PLATE, nine letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Shooting frames at intervals and replaying them fast is a style of photography.

clue.text: Times taken by queen? That's appropriate

parts.note: Anne was a queen of England
X is the multiplication sign, read as times

explanation.surface: A monarch's newspaper reading is described as fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'appropriate' looks like an adjective, but it is the verb meaning seize.
explanation.definitionFit: To annex territory is to seize it, a verb sense of appropriate.

clue.text: Prepare a disguise to come on stage again

indicators.note: a disguise changes the look of something, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor readies a costume to make a second entrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disguise' rearranges PREPARE A.
explanation.definitionFit: To show up once more is to return to view, for an actor back before the audience.

clue.text: One married couple becoming blunt

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a pair is a couple

explanation.surface: A wedded pair grows less sharp with time.
explanation.definitionFit: To weaken or damage something, dulling its edge, is to blunt it.

clue.text: Fur most of the stars presented to ruler

indicators.note: most of a word drops only its final letter

parts.note: astral means of the stars
a khan is a ruler in central Asia

explanation.surface: A star-studded fur coat given to a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most' trims ASTRAL to ASTRA.
explanation.definitionFit: Curly lambskin from Russia is a fur used for coats and hats.

clue.text: Return and bow

definitions.meaning: a return is the profit an investment brings
to bow is to give way, submit

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a profit made and to submit to pressure.

clue.text: Cover girl in a thousand

indicators.note: in says the girl's name sits inside the other letters

parts.note: K, kilo, stands for a thousand
Nora is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A magazine cover girl is one in a thousand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover girl' looks like one phrase, but 'Cover' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A hooded waterproof jacket is a protective cover.

clue.text: Shells, for example, recycled in a fertiliser ingredient

parts.note: shells are one kind of ammunition, informally ammo

indicators.note: recycled material is processed and made into something new, so these two little words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Seashells ground up and reused to enrich the soil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shells, for example' reads as the seaside, but shells are ammunition; 'recycled' rearranges the two little words that follow.
explanation.definitionFit: This pungent nitrogen compound is a key component of many agricultural fertilisers.

clue.text: Sales pitch must have point to get regular order

parts.note: patter is the glib talk of a salesman
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A salesman's spiel needs a sharp point to keep things orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: A design or arrangement that repeats in a regular way is a regular order.

clue.text: Plant in groups, we are told

indicators.note: what we are told is heard rather than seen, so the word for groups is spoken

parts.note: flocks are groups of birds or sheep

explanation.surface: Gardening advice that something grows best in clusters.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden flower with clusters of bright blooms is a plant.

clue.text: Short Spanish king and English queen flirt

indicators.note: something short is cut down, so the king's name loses its final letters

parts.note: Philip was the name of several kings of Spain
taken as written
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the English queen

explanation.surface: Royal gossip: a Spanish king and an English queen trifling with each other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' trims PHILIP to PHIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To trifle with someone's affections, conducting casual love affairs, is to flirt.

clue.text: Outstanding English policeman in an emergency

parts.note: a special constable is a volunteer officer called on to help the regular police, originally in emergencies

explanation.surface: An English officer behaves brilliantly in a crisis.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'special' is a British volunteer police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something particular and exceptional stands out, so it is outstanding.

clue.text: Title role for a cautious type

definitions.text: Title role for a cautious type

parts.words: Title role for a cautious type
parts.note: the name of a play's lead part, read literally, describes someone who is careful

explanation.surface: A theatrical casting note for a wary character.
explanation.walkthrough: The title role of Harold Pinter's play, split in two, is one who takes care.
explanation.definitionFit: A building's custodian also names, read in two halves, a person who is careful.

clue.text: Contract for psychiatrist

definitions.meaning: to contract is to get smaller
slang for a mind doctor, short for headshrinker

explanation.definitionFit: One word both means to become smaller and is slang for a doctor of the mind.

clue.text: Left with one trick badly needed, stick together

indicators.note: something badly done goes wrong, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bridge player left with a single trick badly needed to hold the team together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly needed' rearranges L, ONE and TRICK.
explanation.definitionFit: Parts that fit into one another so they hold firmly stick together.

clue.text: Tom, perhaps, has a curry in cellar

parts.note: a tom is a male cat
taken as written
to curry a horse is to groom it with a comb

explanation.surface: Tom tucks into a curry down in the basement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curry' is not food but grooming a horse with a curry-comb.
explanation.definitionFit: An underground burial chamber is a kind of cellar, loosely.

clue.text: Bishop wary, sounding unclear

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

indicators.note: sounding says the word for wary is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: leery means suspicious, wary

explanation.surface: A cautious bishop mumbles his sermon.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes that are dim and watery see things blurred, so unclear.

clue.text: With bitter leaders, party split down the middle

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of the word bitter

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party

explanation.surface: Riven by resentful leaders, a political party splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut something into two equal halves is to split it down the middle.

clue.text: Fascinating tricks presented without safety measure

indicators.note: without in its old sense means outside, so the tricks wrap round the safety measure

parts.note: magic is the art of conjuring tricks
a net is spread under trapeze artists for safety

explanation.surface: A circus act is thrilling because it is performed with no safety net.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', but in its old sense it means outside, so the tricks wrap round the safety measure.
explanation.definitionFit: Something with strong powers of attraction is captivating, hence fascinating.

clue.text: Ibsen's heroine tucked into ends of cracker and cheese

indicators.note: tucked into says the heroine is placed inside other letters
the ends of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: Hedda Gabler is the heroine of Ibsen's play

explanation.surface: An Ibsen heroine helps herself to cheese and crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: The first and last letters of 'cracker' are C and R, with HEDDA tucked between.
explanation.definitionFit: A hard English cheese from Somerset, named after its village.

clue.text: Time in piece of music acceptable for composer

parts.note: a bar is a short section of music
OK means acceptable

explanation.surface: A performer's timing in a musical passage is deemed satisfactory.
explanation.definitionFit: Béla Bartók was a Hungarian composer.

clue.text: Foundations laid down, start a bus complex

indicators.note: complex means intricate and tangled, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Instructions for a building project involving starting up a bus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complex' rearranges START A BUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Underlying layers deposited beneath the surface are foundations laid down.

clue.text: Heaven for the family in Hay Fever

definitions.meaning: the eccentric family in Noel Coward's comedy Hay Fever have this surname

explanation.definitionFit: The word means perfect happiness and is also the surname of Coward's stage family.

clue.text: Sad song in calamitous key

indicators.note: in says the key is placed inside the word for calamitous

parts.note: dire means dreadful, calamitous
G is a musical key

explanation.surface: A mournful song written in a gloomy key.
explanation.definitionFit: A lament for the dead is a sad song.

clue.text: Author, in spite of editors, taken up

indicators.note: taken up says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A writer is published despite the editors' objections.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'taken up' reads letters upwards: EOFED, inside 'spite of editors', turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English author of Robinson Crusoe.

clue.text: Unsporting? Not this game

parts.note: unfair behaviour is described with the phrase 'not' followed by the name of a game, so the game is the one missing from 'not ...'

explanation.surface: Someone accuses another of poor sportsmanship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's not cricket' is a British idiom for unfair behaviour; cricket is the bat-and-ball game.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying links unfair play to one particular bat-and-ball sport, which is named.

clue.text: Get rid of high responsibility

parts.note: meat that is high has gone off
a load is a burden or responsibility

explanation.surface: Shedding a heavy duty at the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'high' here is gamy, rotten food, not tall.
explanation.definitionFit: To unload or dump something is to get rid of it.

clue.text: Hit by wave, he goes on working

parts.note: to strike is to hit
a breaker is a wave that crashes on the shore

explanation.surface: A man struck by a big wave carries on regardless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hit' and 'wave' look like a seaside accident, but each is a piece of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker who refuses to join industrial action keeps working, crossing picket lines.
